bull.b: The biomarker work advances CNM-Au8 toward a potential ALS NDA and accelerated approval pathway, creating a concrete regulatory milestone. If the evidence supports submission and review, it could shorten development timelines and improve the company’s ability to commercialize its lead program.

An oral lead candidate aimed at neurorepair and neurological function gives Clene a focused development strategy across two serious neurodegenerative diseases. Progress in either ALS or MS could support broader value from the same core therapeutic platform and development expertise.

Extending note maturities and deferring monthly payments can reduce immediate cash pressure while clinical and regulatory work continues. Although these changes do not solve the company’s funding needs, they may provide additional time to pursue milestones and arrange future financing.

bear.b: Heavy operating and free cash outflows show that Clene’s activities are not self-funding and that external capital remains necessary to sustain operations. Continued burn can constrain clinical execution, increase financing dependence, and expose shareholders to recurring funding risk.

Negative equity removes the balance-sheet cushion available to absorb further losses, while debt is large relative to total assets. This combination limits financial flexibility, makes refinancing more important, and can restrict the company’s ability to fund development without additional capital.

Very small revenue and deeply negative operating results indicate that Clene has not established commercial scale or sustainable profitability. Even with a reported revenue rebound, the size of losses relative to revenue means future funding and regulatory success remain essential to the business model.
